Each of K CTAs does an INDEPENDENT local Householder QR of its m/K x b row-block (NO cross-CTA sync during factorization -> fills the device AND halves each chain), then ONE reduction-tree merge (log K syncs per panel, not O(b)). Proven: single-pass TF32 == 6252us == SIMT baseline with simt_sgemm STILL 760us/iter. So 'the tensor cores are idle' is NOT a free lever -- cuBLAS structurally can't use them for this strided op, and 3xTF32 merely runs 3 SIMT passes + splits.

THE WALL (definitive): the only ACCURATE tensor-core option (3xTF32) is SLOWER than cuBLAS SIMT because a hand-written WMMA kernel can't beat cutlass-class GEMM perf and pays 3x the passes; the only FAST option (single-pass TF32) is too INACCURATE (fails the diff guard). cuBLAS itself refuses TC for the in-place STRIDED batched C-=V@Y under g_prec=0 (brief-1 finding, re-confirmed: it's the in-place strided beta=1 OUTPUT, not the math mode -- the W=V^T@C step DOES get TC because it writes a packed buffer). A contiguous-accumulator 3xTF32 (3 cuBLAS TC GEMMs into packed Acc + 1 strided subtract) was rejected by analysis: ~6x the m*rest Acc traffic (~230us bandwidth at the widest dims) > SIMT's 117us, so it's bandwidth-bound and loses. The fused-WMMA is the right traffic structure but the wrong perf class.

THE #1 LEVER (core of the 466us leader's approach). Build a FULLY-FUSED persistent per-matrix tensor-core QR megakernel for the n=512 B=640 GOOD path. Today the good path is ALREADY a partial megakernel (qr_panel_apply_fused_kernel) but it still does the outer-block loop with separate launches + HBM round-trips between OBs, and runs at ~1% of FP8 peak / ~9x off the 3xTF32 roofline (356us) -- so this is a 100x-headroom region, NOT a wall. Goal: ONE persistent kernel, one CTA(or cluster) per matrix, that factors the ENTIRE 512x512 matrix with the panel AND all trailing updates resident in shared memory / registers across ALL outer blocks -- never writing the working matrix back to HBM until done. The 512x512 FP16 working matrix is 512KB (too big for 228KB smem) so tile it: keep the active panel + accumulators on-chip, stream C-tiles via the existing WMMA apply, but eliminate the per-OB kernel relaunch and the inter-OB global sync. Use bf16/FP16 WMMA now (W5 is building the FP8 GEMM substrate you can later swap in). The win is killing the launch/round-trip overhead that makes you 9x off roofline. This is the hardest, highest-value brief -- expect many failed builds; that is the job, keep iterating relentlessly. You know the n512 path deeply from your last 2 briefs. Gate all 12 + invariance(B=1280 3x)+diff-correctness+kernelguard; target n512 shapes (3/7/9/10) far below current. Commit each validated iter with env -u SSH_AUTH_SOCK git commit. Log metric+diff_lines each iter.

On-chip-intermediates HBM saving (~180us/shape) is dwarfed by the ~6x GEMM-throughput loss. cuBLAS trailing GEMMs are NOT the lever.

Also RT=64 sweep (it0->RT=128) showed RT-invariant (~10200us). DEFINITIVE: no single/multi-CTA-per-matrix WMMA structure beats cuBLAS GemmStridedBatchedEx for the OB-wide trailing (S=VtV K=512 + C-=VY M512xN448 are large enough that cuBLAS full-device tiling >> any per-matrix-CTA layout). The brief's 'persistent megakernel keeps trailing on-chip' thesis is disproven for the n512 trailing apply.

Saving 1 launch + the tiny S HBM round-trip (~3us/OB) does not pay for the worse compute. THIRD decisive negative: ANY single-CTA-per-matrix replacement of a cuBLAS GEMM in the n512 good path loses (S=VtV K=512, W=VtC, C-=VY are all big enough that cuBLAS full-device tiling >> 1 CTA).

THE WALL (decisive, 3 independent confirmations + ncu): a SINGLE CTA per matrix CANNOT match cuBLAS GemmStridedBatchedEx for ANY of the n512 good-path GEMMs (S=VtV K=512, W=VtC, C-=VY M512xN448). cuBLAS tiles each GEMM across all 148 SMs (thousands of CTAs); one-CTA-per-matrix uses only B=640 CTAs total for the whole QR (~4 waves) -> ~6-50x less GEMM throughput.
